title: Consumption Playground: Developer Onboarding & Simulator Overview
author: Sofia Patel
body:
Overview

This page describes the Consumption Playground: a developer-focused interactive simulator embedded in the Redwood Console that lets engineers and product teams model realistic inference workloads and see projected cost, latency, and fidelity outcomes before committing to configuration or capacity changes. The Playground is a lightweight UX over the consumption-simulation service (service name: consumption-sim) and integrates Redwood Optimize recommendations, model-catalog profiles, and routing-policy stubs.

Goals

- Give developers a low-friction way to estimate unit economics for feature ideas.
- Surface the most impactful levers (batching, caching, quantization, routing) with credible estimates.
- Produce repeatable simulation artifacts (JSON reports) that can be attached to PRs and procurement requests.

Key capabilities

1) Scenario Builder
- Build scenarios from: sample prompt sets, synthetic traffic generators, or imported traces (OpenTelemetry/JSON).
- Configure request shape: concurrency, distribution of sequence lengths, token entry/exit patterns, and mix of chat vs. generation vs. embeddings.

2) Cost & SLO Simulator
- Estimates per-token and per-request cost using model-catalog cost coefficients and selected quantization profile.
- Simulates latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) using serving-runtime perf profiles and batch scheduling models.
- Simulates fallback behavior: regional failover, cheaper model fallback, or reduced-fidelity response.

3) Fidelity Trade-off Explorer
- Compare quality regressions from quantized variants using embedded eval curves (model-quality delta vs. cost).
- Show suggested guardrails: per-route fidelity budgets, canary thresholds, and auto-rollbacks.

4) Exportable Artifacts
- JSON simulation report, CSV cost breakdown, and a human-readable one-page summary for stakeholder review.

How the Playground models work (high level)

- Input: scenario definition (traffic shape + model + infra hints).
- Engine: consumption-sim calls model-catalog to fetch performance profiles and Redwood Optimize to get quantization/caching recommendations.
- Sampling: synthetic execution traces generated by combining kernel-level throughput curves with batching/caching heuristics.
- Output: cost estimate, latency percentiles, probability of quality regression (based on eval set), and suggested mitigation actions.

Example simulation table

| Scenario | Model | Sequence length distribution | Batch size | Estimated cost/hour | p95 latency | Quality delta | Mitigations |
|---------|-------|-----------------------------|------------|---------------------:|-----------:|--------------|------------|
| Quick Q&A prototype | gpt-open-7b-quant | 90% <= 64, 10% 128-512 | 8 | $3.40 | 220ms | -0.6% | enable prefix cache, enable 8-bit quant profile |
| Embeddings fanout | embed-sim-1 | 100% 256 | 32 | $12.00 | 380ms | n/a | batching + local prefetch proxy |
| Conversational assistant alpha | conv-13b | 60% <= 256, 40% 1024+ | 4 | $7.20 | 410ms | -1.8% | hybrid routing to dedicated pool |

Supported inputs and formats

- Console UI: guided forms and prebuilt templates.
- File import: JSON trace (OpenTelemetry span + token counts) or CSV of sample requests.
- API: POST /v1/simulations with the scenario payload (example below).

Sample API payload (trimmed)

curl -X POST \
  https://console.redwood.inference/simulate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"scenario_name":"alpha-chat-prototype","traffic":{"rps":25,"concurrency":12,"seq_distribution":{"p0_64":0.7,"p65_512":0.25,"p513_plus":0.05}},"model":"conv-13b","quant_profile":"8bit-llm","duration_minutes":60}'

How to run a simulation (developer onboarding flow)

1. Open Redwood Console > Consumption Playground.
2. Choose a template (Quick Q&A, Bulk Embeddings, Conversational Assistant).
3. Select a model variant from the catalog; optionally try a quantized variant.
4. Adjust traffic sliders (RPS, concurrency, sequence length mix).
5. Click Run Simulation. The simulator will take 30–90 seconds for a 60-minute synthetic run.
6. Review the one-page summary and download JSON/CSV artifacts.

Acceptance criteria for the first GA release

- Console UX: three scenario templates + custom scenario editor.
- API: simulation POST/GET endpoints with JSON report generation.
- Integration: calls to model-catalog and redwood-optimize for recommendations.
- Accuracy: median cost estimate within ±15% of small-scale real workload for validated templates.
- Export: JSON report + CSV breakdown + PDF summary.

Rollout plan and milestones

- 2026-03-22: Internal beta (developer preview) launch.
- 2026-04-10: Public beta; collect feedback from top 12 customers and 30 internal teams.
- 2026-05-20: GA release with stable API and 24/7 support.

Ownership and operational notes

- Product owner: Sofia Patel (product).
- Engineering lead: Arjun Rao (eng-platform).
- Infra integration: consumption-sim, model-catalog, redwood-optimize, routing-service, console-sim.
- SLOs: API availability 99.9% (internal beta), simulation job median runtime <= 60s for 60-minute scenarios on standard template.

Limitations & known gaps

- The Playground is a predictor, not a ground-truth engine. Real workloads can deviate due to customer prompt diversity, non-token compute work (retrieval, embedding postprocessing), or network variability.
- Currently does not simulate multi-tenant noisy-neighbor interference on Dedicated pools; this will be added in v1.1.

Security and data handling

- Imported traces and prompt sets are only stored for 30 days by default (configurable per-team).
- Default export artifacts redact personally identifiable tokens and are marked with a retention tag.
- For restricted/regulated customers, run the Playground in Private deployment mode (consumption-sim runs in-customer VPC).

Acceptance checklist for customer-facing demo

1. Demo script with three scenarios (one-page summary ready).
2. Stakeholder one-pager describing estimated unit economics and recommended mitigations.
3. JSON export attached to PR for any config changes.

- scenario_id, created_at, user, model_variant, quant_profile, rps, concurrency, seq_distribution, estimated_tokens, estimated_cost_hour, latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, quality_delta_scores, suggested_mitigations
